text: WiFi card is able either to transmit or receive a signal, but it cannot do both things at the same time. So it cannot transmit and receive at the same time. There are radio cards and points that may do that. Okay, in other technologies, they have more than one transmitter, so they can use one transmitter to transmit and one transmitter to receive, so that they can transmit and receive at the same time. But in WiFi cards, we have only one transmitter, only one. So we can use it either to transmit or to receive. That's half duplex. When you have two transceivers and you can transmit and receive at the same time, that's full duplex. You may say, why can they put an additional transceiver in WiFi cards so that we can transmit and receive at the same time? Well, because WiFi has been conceived as a cheap, low cost technology. So they wanted to include only one transceiver in order to reduce the costs. The drawback is that indeed you have half duplex capabilities. So you cannot transmit and receive at the same time. This is very very very very important in order to understand what we're going to explain later. So keep that in mind. Okay, good.
